No unit from any other build year appears, and the installed base shows KVP-3600 spread across build years from 2015 to 2024, so this is a cohort effect rather than a model-wide or age effect. The failure mode is consistent and physical: IGBT modules discoloured with heat-marked busbars (WO-2026-00480, WO-2026-00696, WO-2026-00702) escalating to units that shut down hard and will not restart (WO-2026-00514, WO-2026-00575, WO-2026-00595). verdict.reasoning: The normalised rate here is 0.073 per installed unit against a peer median of 0.080 - this model is slightly better than its peers, and the cluster exists only because 327 units generate a lot of absolute tickets. This is the clearest illustration in the run of why raw counts mislead: 24 tickets and 113 labour hours look material until divided by installed base. Causes are again external to the inverter - a pinched connector in WO-2024-00069, a chafed home run in WO-2024-00185, no fault found in WO-2025-00084, WO-2025-01248 and WO-2026-00670.
verdict.business_headline: Calderon ground faults run below the fleet average once normalised by installed base - a volume artifact, not a finding.

verdict.reasoning: Residual cleanup from the same March 2025 wind event. The physical finding in the April tickets is a bent limit-switch bracket - mechanical deformation, not calibration drift - in WO-2025-00286, WO-2025-00344 and WO-2025-00375, and WO-2025-00286 opens with a technician noting it is the same as the others that month. Seven of nine members fall in the weeks after the event. H2 would require drift-type language and steady arrivals across the window; instead arrivals collapse after April with only WO-2025-00930 and WO-2026-00073 following later, both of which read as ordinary recalibration. H3 also contributes: eight of nine members carry per-row tags from the same technician identified in CAND-003.
verdict.contradicting_evidence: Two members fall well outside the event window and are genuinely routine recalibration, so the cluster is not purely event-driven. This does not change the verdict but the cluster boundary is imprecise.

population_at_risk.basis: Event-bounded and inflated by per-row logging.

verdict.recommended_action: No action beyond confirming the bent-bracket repairs were captured in the property claim.
